extractedText: Ulsan Must Lead Manufacturing AI Shift, Industry Ministry Official SaysLee Min-woo, Head of Industrial Growth Office at Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy Discusses AI Transformation at 2026 Ulsan Forum Draws Lessons From 16th-Century Age of Exploration Plans to Expand Ulsan's AX Pilots Into Industry-Wide 'M.AX'Finance|Published 2026.09.13. 08:00:05|By Jang Hyun-kilucky@sedaily.com|Summary|SaveAAALee Min-woo, head of the Industrial Growth Office at the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, delivers a keynote speech at the 2026 Ulsan Forum held at the Ulsan Exhibition & Convention Center (UECO) on Nov. 11. Photo by Jang Hyun-kiUlsan, South Korea's largest industrial city, should move first into AX, or artificial intelligence transformation, by tapping its manufacturing data, an industry official said.Lee Min-woo, head of the Industrial Growth Office at the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, made the remarks on the 11th in a lecture titled "Accelerating Ulsan's AX" at the 2026 Ulsan Forum, held at the Ulsan Exhibition & Convention Center (UECO)."Companies are relocating production facilities to China and Southeast Asia, where labor costs are lower," Lee said in the keynote address. "To overcome this, manufacturing needs a fundamental overhaul of its underlying structure."Lee stressed that Ulsan's abundant manufacturing data must be put to use in the age of artificial intelligence. "Ulsan is the first place new ministry officials visit," he said. "There is high-quality manufacturing data here, at the SK (034730) petrochemical complex and the Hyundai Motor (005380) plant, among others." He added, "Just as the countries that pushed through challenges and uncertainty in the 16th-century Age of Exploration seized control of the global economy, we cannot take the lead in the era of AI transformation unless we move first."Lee also highlighted plans to expand Ulsan's AX pilot projects into an industry-wide program dubbed "M.AX," short for manufacturing AX. "In Ulsan, humanoid robots and digital twins are being deployed at SK Energy's plant and at shipbuilding sites," he said. "The ministry will standardize the results from these sites and spread them to plants in other regions."He outlined the ministry's core strategy for M.AX. It involves developing AI solutions that convert the tacit know-how of retiring skilled workers into data, and building a national manufacturing data library to organize that data. The ministry then plans to create a manufacturing AI foundation model and apply it to plants to realize AI factories. "We will also work with local universities to train practitioners who understand both manufacturing and AI," Lee said."What matters is the speed at which Ulsan's potential is turned into actual results," he said. "These voices must not end as a one-off discussion but should lead to concrete projects and policies."The Ulsan Forum was launched at the proposal of SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, who called for local governments and residents to consider the region's future together. Now in its fifth year, this year's forum is being held under the theme "Leading AX, Smart Life Ulsan," with discussions on physical AI and AI for all.#UlsanForum#AITransformation#Manufacturing#SKGroup#AIFactory#UlsanOriginal reporting by Jang Hyun-ki for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
